paper_title: Entanglement entropy of a color flux tube in (2+1)D Yang-Mills theory (Amorosso, 2024, JHEP)
core_reasoning_1:
\section*{Claim}
For a fixed region \(V\), fixed replica index \(q>0\) with \(q\neq 1\), and common ultraviolet regulator \(a\), if the Yang--Mills Renyi entropy with a static \(Q\bar Q\) pair and the vacuum Renyi entropy have the same ultraviolet term, then the flux-tube excess entropy is finite in the continuum limit and equals the difference of finite parts:
\[
\lim_{a\to 0}\widetilde S^{(q)}_{|Q\bar Q}(a)=S^{(q)}_{f,|Q\bar Q}-S^{(q)}_{f}.
\]

\section*{Premises}
\[
\begin{array}{ll}
\text{(P1)} & \widetilde S^{(q)}_{|Q\bar Q}(a):=S^{(q)}_{|Q\bar Q}(a)-S^{(q)}(a).\\[2mm]
\text{(P2)} & S^{(q)}_{|Q\bar Q}(a)=S^{(q)}_{\rm UV}(a)+S^{(q)}_{f,|Q\bar Q}+r_{Q\bar Q}(a).\\[2mm]
\text{(P3)} & S^{(q)}(a)=S^{(q)}_{\rm UV}(a)+S^{(q)}_{f}+r_{0}(a).\\[2mm]
\text{(P4)} & \displaystyle \lim_{a\to 0}r_{Q\bar Q}(a)=0,\qquad \lim_{a\to 0}r_{0}(a)=0.\\[2mm]
\text{(P5)} & S^{(q)}_{f,|Q\bar Q}\in \mathbb{R},\qquad S^{(q)}_{f}\in \mathbb{R}.
\end{array}
\]

\section*{Derivation}
\begin{align}
\widetilde S^{(q)}_{|Q\bar Q}(a)
&=S^{(q)}_{|Q\bar Q}(a)-S^{(q)}(a) && \text{by (P1)}\\
&=\left(S^{(q)}_{\rm UV}(a)+S^{(q)}_{f,|Q\bar Q}+r_{Q\bar Q}(a)\right)
 -\left(S^{(q)}_{\rm UV}(a)+S^{(q)}_{f}+r_{0}(a)\right) && \text{by (P2),(P3)}\\
&=S^{(q)}_{\rm UV}(a)-S^{(q)}_{\rm UV}(a)+S^{(q)}_{f,|Q\bar Q}-S^{(q)}_{f}+r_{Q\bar Q}(a)-r_0(a) && \text{expansion}\\
&=S^{(q)}_{f,|Q\bar Q}-S^{(q)}_{f}+r_{Q\bar Q}(a)-r_0(a) && \text{cancellation of the common UV term}\\
\lim_{a\to 0}\widetilde S^{(q)}_{|Q\bar Q}(a)
&=S^{(q)}_{f,|Q\bar Q}-S^{(q)}_{f}+\lim_{a\to 0}r_{Q\bar Q}(a)-\lim_{a\to 0}r_0(a) && \text{limit of a finite sum}\\
&=S^{(q)}_{f,|Q\bar Q}-S^{(q)}_{f} && \text{by (P4)}.
\end{align}

\section*{Final Result}
\[
\boxed{\displaystyle \lim_{a\to 0}\widetilde S^{(q)}_{|Q\bar Q}(a)=S^{(q)}_{f,|Q\bar Q}-S^{(q)}_{f}\in \mathbb{R}}
\]
\hfill$\blacksquare$
core_reasoning_2:
\section*{Claim}
If the reduced density matrix associated with a gauge-invariant algebra is block diagonal over superselection sectors,
\[
\rho_A=\bigoplus_{k=1}^{m}p_k\rho_{A_k},
\]
where \(p_k\geq 0\), \(\sum_{k=1}^{m}p_k=1\), and \(\operatorname{Tr}\rho_{A_k}=1\), then its von Neumann entropy decomposes into a boundary classical Shannon term plus a bulk quantum term:
\[
S_E(\rho_A)=-\sum_{k=1}^{m}p_k\log p_k+\sum_{k=1}^{m}p_kS(\rho_{A_k}).
\]

\section*{Premises}
\[
\begin{array}{ll}
\text{(P1)} & \rho_A=\operatorname{diag}(p_1\rho_{A_1},\ldots,p_m\rho_{A_m}).\\[1mm]
\text{(P2)} & p_k\geq 0,\quad \displaystyle\sum_{k=1}^{m}p_k=1,\quad \operatorname{Tr}\rho_{A_k}=1.\\[2mm]
\text{(P3)} & S_E(\rho_A):=-\operatorname{Tr}(\rho_A\log \rho_A).\\[1mm]
\text{(P4)} & S(\rho_{A_k}):=-\operatorname{Tr}(\rho_{A_k}\log \rho_{A_k}).\\[1mm]
\text{(P5)} & \log\operatorname{diag}(B_1,\ldots,B_m)=\operatorname{diag}(\log B_1,
\ldots,\log B_m) \text{ for positive blocks}.\\[1mm]
\text{(P6)} & \log(p_k\rho_{A_k})=(\log p_k)I_k+\log\rho_{A_k}\quad \text{for }p_k>0.
\end{array}
\]
Terms with \(p_k=0\) are defined by the limit \(p_k\log p_k\to 0\).

\section*{Derivation}
\begin{align}
S_E(\rho_A)
&=-\operatorname{Tr}(\rho_A\log\rho_A) && \text{by (P3)}\\
&=-\sum_{k=1}^{m}\operatorname{Tr}\left(p_k\rho_{A_k}\log(p_k\rho_{A_k})\right) && \text{by (P1),(P5)}\\
&=-\sum_{k=1}^{m}\operatorname{Tr}\left(p_k\rho_{A_k}\left((\log p_k)I_k+\log\rho_{A_k}\right)\right) && \text{by (P6)}\\
&=-\sum_{k=1}^{m}p_k(\log p_k)\operatorname{Tr}(\rho_{A_k})-
\sum_{k=1}^{m}p_k\operatorname{Tr}(\rho_{A_k}\log\rho_{A_k}) && \text{linearity of trace}\\
&=-\sum_{k=1}^{m}p_k\log p_k+
\sum_{k=1}^{m}p_k\left[-\operatorname{Tr}(\rho_{A_k}\log\rho_{A_k})\right] && \text{by (P2)}\\
&=-\sum_{k=1}^{m}p_k\log p_k+\sum_{k=1}^{m}p_kS(\rho_{A_k}) && \text{by (P4)}.
\end{align}

\section*{Final Result}
\[
\boxed{\displaystyle S_E(\rho_A)=-\sum_{k=1}^{m}p_k\log p_k+\sum_{k=1}^{m}p_kS(\rho_{A_k})}
\]
\hfill$\blacksquare$
core_reasoning_3:
\section*{Claim}
For the same block diagonal reduced density matrix
\[
\rho_A=\bigoplus_{k=1}^{m}p_k\rho_{A_k},
\]
the \(q\)-Renyi entropy with \(q>0\), \(q\neq 1\), is
\[
S^{(q)}(\rho_A)=\frac{1}{q-1}\left(-\log\sum_{k=1}^{m}p_k^q-\log\sum_{k=1}^{m}a_k^{(q)}\operatorname{Tr}(\rho_{A_k}^q)\right),
\]
where
\[
a_k^{(q)}:=\frac{p_k^q}{\sum_{i=1}^{m}p_i^q}.
\]

\section*{Premises}
\[
\begin{array}{ll}
\text{(P1)} & \rho_A=\operatorname{diag}(p_1\rho_{A_1},\ldots,p_m\rho_{A_m}).\\[1mm]
\text{(P2)} & p_k\geq 0,\quad \displaystyle\sum_{k=1}^{m}p_k=1,\quad \operatorname{Tr}\rho_{A_k}=1.\\[2mm]
\text{(P3)} & S^{(q)}(\rho_A):=\displaystyle\frac{1}{1-q}\log\operatorname{Tr}(\rho_A^q),\quad q>0,\quad q\neq 1.\\[2mm]
\text{(P4)} & \left[\operatorname{diag}(B_1,
\ldots,B_m)\right]^q=\operatorname{diag}(B_1^q,
\ldots,B_m^q) \text{ for positive blocks}.\\[1mm]
\text{(P5)} & A_q:=\displaystyle\sum_{i=1}^{m}p_i^q,\qquad a_k^{(q)}:=\displaystyle\frac{p_k^q}{A_q}.
\end{array}
\]

\section*{Derivation}
\begin{align}
\rho_A^q
&=\operatorname{diag}\left((p_1\rho_{A_1})^q,\ldots,(p_m\rho_{A_m})^q\right) && \text{by (P1),(P4)}\\
&=\operatorname{diag}\left(p_1^q\rho_{A_1}^q,\ldots,p_m^q\rho_{A_m}^q\right) && \text{scalar powers commute}\\
\operatorname{Tr}(\rho_A^q)
&=\sum_{k=1}^{m}p_k^q\operatorname{Tr}(\rho_{A_k}^q) && \text{trace of block diagonal matrix}\\
&=\left(\sum_{i=1}^{m}p_i^q\right)\sum_{k=1}^{m}\frac{p_k^q}{\sum_{i=1}^{m}p_i^q}\operatorname{Tr}(\rho_{A_k}^q) && \text{multiply and divide by }A_q\\
&=A_q\sum_{k=1}^{m}a_k^{(q)}\operatorname{Tr}(\rho_{A_k}^q) && \text{by (P5)}\\
S^{(q)}(\rho_A)
&=\frac{1}{1-q}\log\left(A_q\sum_{k=1}^{m}a_k^{(q)}\operatorname{Tr}(\rho_{A_k}^q)\right) && \text{by (P3)}\\
&=-\frac{1}{q-1}\left(\log A_q+\log\sum_{k=1}^{m}a_k^{(q)}\operatorname{Tr}(\rho_{A_k}^q)\right) && \text{since }\frac{1}{1-q}=-\frac{1}{q-1}\\
&=\frac{1}{q-1}\left(-\log\sum_{k=1}^{m}p_k^q-\log\sum_{k=1}^{m}a_k^{(q)}\operatorname{Tr}(\rho_{A_k}^q)\right) && \text{by (P5)}.
\end{align}

\section*{Final Result}
\[
\boxed{\displaystyle S^{(q)}(\rho_A)=\frac{1}{q-1}\left(-\log\sum_{k=1}^{m}p_k^q-\log\sum_{k=1}^{m}a_k^{(q)}\operatorname{Tr}(\rho_{A_k}^q)\right)}
\]
\hfill$\blacksquare$
core_reasoning_4:
\section*{Claim}
For a \(U(1)\) boundary site \(A\), the projected partial wave functional
\[
\Psi_{V,\lambda_A}:=\int_{0}^{2\pi}\frac{d\alpha}{2\pi}\,e^{i\lambda_A\alpha}
\Psi_V(e^{i\alpha}U_{AB},e^{i\alpha}U_{AC},e^{i\alpha}U_{AD},\ldots)
\]
is an eigenvector of the total electric flux from \(A\) into \(V\), and transforms covariantly under a boundary gauge transformation:
\[
(E_A)_V\Psi_{V,\lambda_A}=\lambda_A\Psi_{V,\lambda_A},
\qquad
\Psi_{V,\lambda_A}((U_V)^{e^{i\beta}})=e^{-i\lambda_A\beta}\Psi_{V,\lambda_A}(U_V).
\]

\section*{Premises}
\[
\begin{array}{ll}
\text{(P1)} & U_{AX}=e^{i\theta_{AX}}\quad\text{for }X\in\{B,C,D\}.\\[1mm]
\text{(P2)} & \displaystyle (E_A)_V:=i\left(\frac{\partial}{\partial\theta_{AB}}+\frac{\partial}{\partial\theta_{AC}}+\frac{\partial}{\partial\theta_{AD}}\right).\\[3mm]
\text{(P3)} & \displaystyle \Psi_{V,\lambda_A}:=\int_{0}^{2\pi}\frac{d\alpha}{2\pi}e^{i\lambda_A\alpha}
\Psi_V(e^{i\alpha}U_{AB},e^{i\alpha}U_{AC},e^{i\alpha}U_{AD},\ldots).\\[3mm]
\text{(P4)} & \lambda_A\in\mathbb{Z},\quad \Psi_V(e^{i(\alpha+2\pi)}U_{AB},e^{i(\alpha+2\pi)}U_{AC},e^{i(\alpha+2\pi)}U_{AD},\ldots)=\\
&\qquad \Psi_V(e^{i\alpha}U_{AB},e^{i\alpha}U_{AC},e^{i\alpha}U_{AD},\ldots).\\[2mm]
\text{(P5)} & (U_V)^{e^{i\beta}}\text{ means }U_{AB},U_{AC},U_{AD}\text{ are replaced by }e^{i\beta}U_{AB},e^{i\beta}U_{AC},e^{i\beta}U_{AD}.
\end{array}
\]

\section*{Derivation}
Define
\[
F(\alpha):=\Psi_V(e^{i\alpha}U_{AB},e^{i\alpha}U_{AC},e^{i\alpha}U_{AD},\ldots).
\]
Then
\begin{align}
(E_A)_V\Psi_{V,\lambda_A}
&=i\int_{0}^{2\pi}\frac{d\alpha}{2\pi}e^{i\lambda_A\alpha}
\left(\frac{\partial}{\partial\theta_{AB}}+\frac{\partial}{\partial\theta_{AC}}+\frac{\partial}{\partial\theta_{AD}}\right)F(\alpha) && \text{by (P2),(P3)}\\
&=i\int_{0}^{2\pi}\frac{d\alpha}{2\pi}e^{i\lambda_A\alpha}\frac{dF(\alpha)}{d\alpha} && \text{chain rule using (P1)}\\
&=i\left[\frac{e^{i\lambda_A\alpha}F(\alpha)}{2\pi}\right]_{0}^{2\pi}
-i\int_{0}^{2\pi}\frac{d\alpha}{2\pi}(i\lambda_A)e^{i\lambda_A\alpha}F(\alpha) && \text{integration by parts}\\
&=0+\lambda_A\int_{0}^{2\pi}\frac{d\alpha}{2\pi}e^{i\lambda_A\alpha}F(\alpha) && \text{by (P4)}\\
&=\lambda_A\Psi_{V,\lambda_A} && \text{by (P3)}.
\end{align}
For the gauge transformation,
\begin{align}
\Psi_{V,\lambda_A}((U_V)^{e^{i\beta}})
&=\int_{0}^{2\pi}\frac{d\alpha}{2\pi}e^{i\lambda_A\alpha}F(\alpha+\beta) && \text{by (P3),(P5)}\\
&=\int_{\beta}^{2\pi+\beta}\frac{d\alpha'}{2\pi}e^{i\lambda_A(\alpha'-\beta)}F(\alpha') && \text{substitute }\alpha':=\alpha+\beta\\
&=e^{-i\lambda_A\beta}\int_{0}^{2\pi}\frac{d\alpha'}{2\pi}e^{i\lambda_A\alpha'}F(\alpha') && \text{by }2\pi\text{-periodicity in (P4)}\\
&=e^{-i\lambda_A\beta}\Psi_{V,\lambda_A} && \text{by (P3)}.
\end{align}

\section*{Final Result}
\[
\boxed{\displaystyle (E_A)_V\Psi_{V,\lambda_A}=\lambda_A\Psi_{V,\lambda_A},\qquad
\Psi_{V,\lambda_A}((U_V)^{e^{i\beta}})=e^{-i\lambda_A\beta}\Psi_{V,\lambda_A}(U_V)}
\]
\hfill$\blacksquare$
core_reasoning_5:
\section*{Claim}
For an integer replica number \(q\geq 2\), a static quark at \(\vec x\), and a static antiquark at \(\vec y\), assume the Polyakov-loop correlator ratio \(R_q\) is positive. Then the flux-tube Renyi excess entropy is the logarithm of a manifestly gauge-invariant ratio of Polyakov-loop correlators:
\[
R_q^g=R_q,
\qquad
\widetilde S^{(q)}_{|Q_{\vec x}\bar Q_{\vec y}}
=-\frac{1}{q-1}\log R_q,
\]
where
\[
R_q:=
\frac{\left\langle\prod_{r=1}^{q}\operatorname{Tr}P^{(r)}_{\vec x}\operatorname{Tr}P^{(r)\dagger}_{\vec y}\right\rangle}{\left\langle\operatorname{Tr}P_{\vec x}\operatorname{Tr}P_{\vec y}^{\dagger}\right\rangle^{q}}.
\]

\section*{Premises}
\[
\begin{array}{ll}
\text{(P1)} & q\in\mathbb{Z},\quad q\geq 2.\\[1mm]
\text{(P2)} & S^{(q)}(\rho):=\displaystyle\frac{1}{1-q}\log\operatorname{Tr}(\rho^q).\\[2mm]
\text{(P3)} & \widetilde S^{(q)}_{|Q_{\vec x}\bar Q_{\vec y}}:=S^{(q)}_{|Q_{\vec x}\bar Q_{\vec y}}-S^{(q)}.\\[2mm]
\text{(P4)} & \displaystyle \operatorname{Tr}\left[(\rho_V|Q_{\vec x}\bar Q_{\vec y})^q\right]
=\frac{Z^{(q)}_{|Q_{\vec x}\bar Q_{\vec y}}}{\left(Z_{|Q_{\vec x}\bar Q_{\vec y}}\right)^q}.\\[3mm]
\text{(P5)} & \displaystyle \operatorname{Tr}(\rho_V^q)=\frac{Z^{(q)}}{Z^q}.\\[3mm]
\text{(P6)} & \displaystyle R_q:=
\frac{\left\langle\prod_{r=1}^{q}\operatorname{Tr}P^{(r)}_{\vec x}\operatorname{Tr}P^{(r)\dagger}_{\vec y}\right\rangle}{\left\langle\operatorname{Tr}P_{\vec x}\operatorname{Tr}P_{\vec y}^{\dagger}\right\rangle^{q}},\quad R_q>0.\\[5mm]
\text{(P7)} & \displaystyle \frac{Z^{(q)}_{|Q_{\vec x}\bar Q_{\vec y}}}{\left(Z_{|Q_{\vec x}\bar Q_{\vec y}}\right)^q}=R_q\frac{Z^{(q)}}{Z^q}.\\[3mm]
\text{(P8)} & \displaystyle P_{\vec z}^{(r)}\mapsto G_{\vec z}^{(r)}P_{\vec z}^{(r)}\left(G_{\vec z}^{(r)}\right)^{-1}\quad\text{under a gauge transformation}.\\[2mm]
\text{(P9)} & \displaystyle \operatorname{Tr}(ABA^{-1})=\operatorname{Tr}(B)\quad\text{for every invertible }A\text{ and square }B.
\end{array}
\]

\section*{Derivation}
First show gauge invariance of the correlator ratio. For each replica \(r\),
\begin{align}
\operatorname{Tr}P_{\vec x}^{(r)}
&\mapsto \operatorname{Tr}\left(G_{\vec x}^{(r)}P_{\vec x}^{(r)}\left(G_{\vec x}^{(r)}\right)^{-1}\right) && \text{by (P8)}\\
&=\operatorname{Tr}P_{\vec x}^{(r)} && \text{by (P9)},\\
\operatorname{Tr}P_{\vec y}^{(r)\dagger}
&\mapsto \operatorname{Tr}\left(G_{\vec y}^{(r)}P_{\vec y}^{(r)\dagger}\left(G_{\vec y}^{(r)}\right)^{-1}\right) && \text{by (P8)}\\
&=\operatorname{Tr}P_{\vec y}^{(r)\dagger} && \text{by (P9)}.
\end{align}
Therefore
\begin{align}
\left\langle\prod_{r=1}^{q}\operatorname{Tr}P^{(r)}_{\vec x}\operatorname{Tr}P^{(r)\dagger}_{\vec y}\right\rangle
&\mapsto
\left\langle\prod_{r=1}^{q}\operatorname{Tr}P^{(r)}_{\vec x}\operatorname{Tr}P^{(r)\dagger}_{\vec y}\right\rangle && \text{product of invariant factors},\\
\left\langle\operatorname{Tr}P_{\vec x}\operatorname{Tr}P_{\vec y}^{\dagger}\right\rangle^{q}
&\mapsto
\left\langle\operatorname{Tr}P_{\vec x}\operatorname{Tr}P_{\vec y}^{\dagger}\right\rangle^{q} && \text{same argument},\\
R_q^g&=R_q && \text{by (P6)}.
\end{align}
Now compute the excess entropy:
\begin{align}
S^{(q)}_{|Q_{\vec x}\bar Q_{\vec y}}
&=\frac{1}{1-q}\log\operatorname{Tr}\left[(\rho_V|Q_{\vec x}\bar Q_{\vec y})^q\right] && \text{by (P2)}\\
&=\frac{1}{1-q}\log\left(\frac{Z^{(q)}_{|Q_{\vec x}\bar Q_{\vec y}}}{\left(Z_{|Q_{\vec x}\bar Q_{\vec y}}\right)^q}\right) && \text{by (P4)}\\
&=\frac{1}{1-q}\log\left(R_q\frac{Z^{(q)}}{Z^q}\right) && \text{by (P7)}\\
&=\frac{1}{1-q}\log R_q+\frac{1}{1-q}\log\left(\frac{Z^{(q)}}{Z^q}\right) && \text{log product rule, valid since }R_q>0,\\
S^{(q)}
&=\frac{1}{1-q}\log\operatorname{Tr}(\rho_V^q) && \text{by (P2)}\\
&=\frac{1}{1-q}\log\left(\frac{Z^{(q)}}{Z^q}\right) && \text{by (P5)}.
\end{align}
Subtracting gives
\begin{align}
\widetilde S^{(q)}_{|Q_{\vec x}\bar Q_{\vec y}}
&=S^{(q)}_{|Q_{\vec x}\bar Q_{\vec y}}-S^{(q)} && \text{by (P3)}\\
&=\left[\frac{1}{1-q}\log R_q+\frac{1}{1-q}\log\left(\frac{Z^{(q)}}{Z^q}\right)\right]
-\frac{1}{1-q}\log\left(\frac{Z^{(q)}}{Z^q}\right) && \text{substitution}\\
&=\frac{1}{1-q}\log R_q && \text{cancellation of the vacuum replica factor}\\
&=-\frac{1}{q-1}\log R_q && \text{because }1-q=-(q-1).
\end{align}

\section*{Final Result}
\[
\boxed{\displaystyle R_q^g=R_q,\qquad
\widetilde S^{(q)}_{|Q_{\vec x}\bar Q_{\vec y}}
=-\frac{1}{q-1}\log
\frac{\left\langle\prod_{r=1}^{q}\operatorname{Tr}P^{(r)}_{\vec x}\operatorname{Tr}P^{(r)\dagger}_{\vec y}\right\rangle}{\left\langle\operatorname{Tr}P_{\vec x}\operatorname{Tr}P_{\vec y}^{\dagger}\right\rangle^{q}}}
\]
\hfill$\blacksquare$
core_reasoning_7:
\section*{Claim}
For the discretized thin-string Hamiltonian
\[
H=a^TXa+p^TQp,
\]
with \(X=Y^TY\), the linear transformations used in the paper diagonalize the Hamiltonian and give the Gaussian ground-state matrix
\[
M=Y^T(YQY^T)^{-1/2}Y.
\]
Equivalently,
\[
H=c^Tc+s^TDs,
\qquad
\Psi(a)\propto \exp\left[-\frac{1}{2}a^TMa\right].
\]

\section*{Premises}
\[
\begin{array}{ll}
\text{(P1)} & H=a^TXa+p^TQp,\quad X=X^T>0,\quad Q=Q^T>0.\\[1mm]
\text{(P2)} & X=Y^TY\quad\text{with }Y\text{ invertible}.\\[1mm]
\text{(P3)} & b:=Ya,
\qquad r:=(Y^{-1})^Tp.\\[1mm]
\text{(P4)} & Z^TZ=ZZ^T=I,
\qquad D:=ZYQY^TZ^T\text{ is diagonal and positive}.\\[1mm]
\text{(P5)} & s:=Zr,
\qquad c:=(Z^{-1})^Tb.\\[1mm]
\text{(P6)} & \text{For one coordinate }x\text{ and momentum }-i\partial_x,\text{ if }d>0,\text{ then }h:=x^2+d(-\partial_x^2).\\[1mm]
\text{(P7)} & \displaystyle \text{If }f_d(x):=\exp\left(-\frac{x^2}{2\sqrt d}\right),\text{ then }\partial_x^2 f_d(x)=\left(\frac{x^2}{d}-\frac{1}{\sqrt d}\right)f_d(x).
\end{array}
\]

\section*{Derivation}
First transform the quadratic form:
\begin{align}
a^TXa
&=a^TY^TYa && \text{by (P2)}\\
&=(Ya)^T(Ya) && \text{transpose rule}\\
&=b^Tb && \text{by (P3)}.
\end{align}
For the momentum term, solve \(p=Y^Tr\) from \(r=(Y^{-1})^Tp\). Then
\begin{align}
p^TQp
&=(Y^Tr)^TQ(Y^Tr) && \text{substitute }p=Y^Tr\\
&=r^TYQY^Tr && \text{transpose rule}\\
&=r^TZ^TDZr && \text{by (P4)}\\
&=(Zr)^TD(Zr) && \text{orthogonality of }Z\\
&=s^TDs && \text{by (P5)}.
\end{align}
Also, since \(Z^{-1}=Z^T\),
\begin{align}
c=(Z^{-1})^Tb=Zb.
\end{align}
Thus \(b^Tb=c^Tc\), and
\begin{align}
H&=c^Tc+s^TDs. && \text{combine the transformed terms}
\end{align}
Now let \(D=\operatorname{diag}(d_1,\ldots,d_n)\), \(d_i>0\), and consider
\[
\Psi(c):=\prod_{i=1}^{n}\exp\left(-\frac{c_i^2}{2\sqrt{d_i}}\right)=\exp\left(-\frac{1}{2}c^TD^{-1/2}c\right).
\]
For each mode,
\begin{align}
\left(c_i^2+d_i(-\partial_{c_i}^2)\right)\exp\left(-\frac{c_i^2}{2\sqrt{d_i}}\right)
&=\left(c_i^2-d_i\left(\frac{c_i^2}{d_i}-\frac{1}{\sqrt{d_i}}\right)\right)\exp\left(-\frac{c_i^2}{2\sqrt{d_i}}\right) && \text{by (P7)}\\
&=\sqrt{d_i}\exp\left(-\frac{c_i^2}{2\sqrt{d_i}}\right) && \text{algebra}.
\end{align}
Hence the Gaussian exponent matrix in \(c\)-coordinates is \(D^{-1/2}\). Since
\begin{align}
c&=ZYa && \text{by (P3),(P5)},\\
c^TD^{-1/2}c
&=a^TY^TZ^TD^{-1/2}ZYa && \text{substitute }c=ZYa\\
&=a^TY^T(YQY^T)^{-1/2}Ya && \text{because }D=ZYQY^TZ^T,
\end{align}
we identify
\begin{align}
M:=Y^T(YQY^T)^{-1/2}Y.
\end{align}

\section*{Final Result}
\[
\boxed{\displaystyle H=c^Tc+s^TDs,\qquad \Psi(a)\propto\exp\left[-\frac{1}{2}a^TY^T(YQY^T)^{-1/2}Ya\right]}
\]
\hfill$\blacksquare$
core_reasoning_8:
\section*{Claim}
For the fully cut discretized thin-string model with \(N\) longitudinal basis intervals and \(N=L/\epsilon\), the Gaussian replica formula implies
\[
S^{(2)}=\frac{1}{2}\log\det M_2.
\]
Combining this with the paper's stated large-\(N\) thin-string behavior gives
\[
S^{(2)}=\frac{1}{4}\log\frac{L}{\epsilon}+O(1)\qquad (L/\epsilon\to\infty).
\]

\section*{Premises}
\[
\begin{array}{ll}
\text{(P1)} & \displaystyle S^{(q)}:=\frac{1}{1-q}\log\operatorname{Tr}(\rho^q),\quad q>0,
\quad q\neq 1.\\[2mm]
\text{(P2)} & \displaystyle \operatorname{Tr}(\rho^n)=\frac{1}{\sqrt{\det M_n}},\quad \det M_n>0,\quad \operatorname{Tr}\rho=1.\\[3mm]
\text{(P3)} & \displaystyle S^{(2)}(N)=\frac{1}{4}\log N+F_N,\quad F_N=O(1)\quad\text{as }N\to\infty.\\[2mm]
\text{(P4)} & \displaystyle N:=\frac{L}{\epsilon},\quad L>0,
\quad \epsilon>0,
\quad \frac{L}{\epsilon}\to\infty.\\[3mm]
\text{(P5)} & \displaystyle \log(x^{-1/2})=-\frac{1}{2}\log x\quad\text{for }x>0.\\[2mm]
\text{(P6)} & \displaystyle \text{If }F_N=O(1)\text{ and }N=L/\epsilon,\text{ then }F_{L/\epsilon}=O(1).
\end{array}
\]

\section*{Derivation}
Set \(q=2\) in the Renyi definition:
\begin{align}
S^{(2)}
&=\frac{1}{1-2}\log\operatorname{Tr}(\rho^2) && \text{by (P1)}\\
&=-\log\operatorname{Tr}(\rho^2) && \text{since }1-2=-1\\
&=-\log\left(\frac{1}{\sqrt{\det M_2}}\right) && \text{by (P2)}\\
&=-\log\left((\det M_2)^{-1/2}\right) && \text{rewrite the square root}\\
&=-\left(-\frac{1}{2}\log\det M_2\right) && \text{by (P5)}\\
&=\frac{1}{2}\log\det M_2 && \text{algebra}.
\end{align}
For the large-\(N\) fully cut string,
\begin{align}
S^{(2)}(N)
&=\frac{1}{4}\log N+F_N && \text{by (P3)}\\
&=\frac{1}{4}\log\left(\frac{L}{\epsilon}\right)+F_{L/\epsilon} && \text{substitute }N=L/\epsilon\text{ from (P4)}\\
&=\frac{1}{4}\log\left(\frac{L}{\epsilon}\right)+O(1) && \text{by (P6)}.
\end{align}
Combining the exact Gaussian replica identity with the large-\(N\) behavior gives
\begin{align}
\frac{1}{2}\log\det M_2
&=S^{(2)} && \text{from the first derived identity}\\
&=\frac{1}{4}\log\left(\frac{L}{\epsilon}\right)+O(1) && \text{from the second derived identity}.
\end{align}

\section*{Final Result}
\[
\boxed{\displaystyle S^{(2)}=\frac{1}{2}\log\det M_2
=\frac{1}{4}\log\frac{L}{\epsilon}+O(1)\qquad (L/\epsilon\to\infty)}
\]
\hfill$\blacksquare$
